resolved_findings.title: A failed registry insertion left an unretained scene pointer for later light cleanup
resolved_findings.trigger: First attach to the fresh light publishes its +178 entry/count, then SceneNodeRegistry::insert_00b83700 throws during entry allocation or host bindings_.emplace before attach performs its final scene retain.
evidence: src/light_scene_retention.cpp:41..46 publishes entry, increments count, calls add_scene_node_if_type_00b83d50, then references.fetch_add(1).
Native 00B7C080 writes entry; 00B7C082 increments count; 00B7C089 calls 00B83D50; 00B7C092 calls InterlockedIncrement. This original ordering is retained.
src/scene_attachment.cpp:163..167 entry allocation, list length check, and bindings_.emplace can throw before the registry links are committed.
The original probe declares MeshLightShutdown before resource and scene-slot guards. Unwinding destroys the slot guard, then creator resource guard, before light cleanup.
With only creator+slot references present, those two releases free the scene; the light destructor then reads the freed pointer from its published +178 entry.
resolved_findings.resolution: Catch only around this isolated attach. If actual +178 count is one and entry zero equals resource, take one real scene reference before rethrowing. The published backlink then owns the reference expected by ordinary native light cleanup.
source_proof_conditions: Fresh native light constructor leaves +178 count zero.
This call is recurse=false and has no shadow/hierarchy or mutating type callbacks.
MeshLightSceneRuntime predicates call complete noexcept descriptor comparisons.
Registry insertion can throw before attach retain; no operation after that final retain throws on this nonrecursive path.
A caught count-one matching entry therefore lacks exactly one retain. If reserve failed before publication, count remains zero and no compensation occurs.
After compensation scene count is three; slot and creator cleanup reduce to one, then native light unregister/release reduces to zero and returns the actual pool slot.
The native attach routine, native callback order, and native component exception behavior remain unchanged.
resolved_findings.validation: Correction source-reviewed; ordinary strict build and installed probe rerun by primary passed. No allocation-failure injection was performed.
resolved_findings.not_a_general_rollback: This guard relies on the documented fresh, single-attach, nonreentrant probe state. It is not a general transaction wrapper for arbitrary native attach calls.

details: Light constructor preserves effective specular+194, mode3 diffuse+1B4, specular scale+1DC, and direction+1E0 raw preimages.

reviewed_invariants.conclusion: Confirmed for stable initialized descriptors in this isolated domain.
details: Explicit zero-filled descriptor/guard preimages are initialized through the shared TypeIdCounterLifetime before SceneAttachmentRuntime copies the resulting light registry token.
Directional callbacks accept directional/light/node/root tokens, light-phase callbacks accept light/node/root, and node-phase callbacks accept node/root.
The deleting wrapper enters directional phase, light destruction installs light predicate plus light attach/remove callbacks, then node destruction installs node predicate plus base node callbacks.
MeshLightTypes is declared before scenes, destruction runtime, pool, native light and resource; those dependent locals are cleaned up while descriptors and bootstrap are still alive.
The empty c3dObject token tuple is not used by this light-only path; no c3dObject is bound or dispatched.
No descriptor reinitialization or mutation after bootstrap occurs in this probe; this review does not extend the copied registry token to arbitrary dynamic token changes.

reviewed_invariants.topic: Real pool return and normal scene/ambient cleanup
reviewed_invariants.conclusion: Confirmed by source and primary installed assertions.
details: Pool allocates an actual 1F0-byte slot with native slab index at +1EC; node prefix and light tail preserve that final index word.
Before companion ownership transfer, MeshLightSlotShutdown returns the raw slot on setup failure. After binding, the pointer is cleared and MeshLightShutdown owns explicit native deletion.

Successful deletion drains the actual scene backlinks, releases any actual retained shadow (none here), frees array/name storage, ends node/tail lifetimes, forgets the scene binding and returns the same pool slot for flag one.
Explicit close clears its owner pointer to avoid a second deletion on normal scope exit. Explicit scene-slot clear and creator release finish scene and ambient destruction.
The probe trims the pool and asserts slab_count zero and recursion zero, providing evidence that the actual returned slot made the slab empty.

reviewed_invariants.topic: Shared lifetime routing and shutdown callback lifetime
reviewed_invariants.conclusion: Confirmed for the two concrete registered owner kinds in this domain.
details: Particle clock and type counter register with the same SingletonLifetimeDomain; the callback identifies the type counter by its actual currently published slot identity and otherwise dispatches the particle owner.
Only these two owner kinds register in the reviewed path. This identity switch is not advertised as a general native virtual dispatcher.
Callback context, particle adapter, type adapter, raw slots and string pool are created before MeshSingletonShutdown, so guard shutdown occurs while all are alive.
The manager removes the last registered entry before invoking destruction, giving type-counter cleanup before particle cleanup on this creation order.
Type deleting destructor clears its global without accessing MeshLightTypes descriptors; those local descriptors may already have expired safely after light/scene cleanup.
Explicit shutdown clears published manager and slots; subsequent guard/domain destructor shutdown is a no-op. Installed assertions observe exactly one counter and one particle destruction.

reviewed_invariants.topic: Other setup failures and native exception boundaries
reviewed_invariants.conclusion: No additional newly actionable issue identified within the isolated path; native component limitations retained.
details: Pool initializer has its own table/critical-section/list unwind before the outer pool guard exists.
First-slab allocation failure leaves the native recursion/lock state for the pool guard destructor to drain; this fresh pool does not enter later table-growth failure after allocating a slab.
Node setup uses an empty name and fresh null arrays/retained fields; the pre-transfer raw-slot guard covers setup failure before light native cleanup is armed.

If later upload returns failure or throws after complete attach, the scene has its backlink reference, allowing resource guards before light cleanup; the resolved finding covers the incomplete-attach exception.
Existing scene constructor intentionally preserves native ambient/backlink exception behavior; this review does not reclassify it as a general strong exception guarantee.
No injected destructor callback failures, concurrent mutation, arbitrary reentrant hierarchy mutation or low-memory execution were tested by this review.
